clue.text: Old Italian PM describing love, having caught twins in leather

indicators.note: having something caught inside means holding it, so the twin letters sit within the outer pieces

parts.note: Aldo Moro was Prime Minister of Italy, killed in 1978
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught; twins make two of it

explanation.surface: An Italian statesman of old talks of romance while carrying two babies in leather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' (going round) is used loosely: O sits after MORO, with CC slotted between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Morocco is a fine goatskin leather used in bookbinding, named after the country.

clue.text: See 20
Logic not referring to a daughter then?

parts.note: re means about, referring to
with not before it, the child meant is the other kind, a son

explanation.surface: Is reasoning ever not about a daughter?
explanation.walkthrough: 'not referring to a daughter' is read as about a son: RE A SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason is the faculty of logical thought; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Mushroom ring shining on group of whales — or squid, say?

parts.note: a cep is an edible mushroom, the porcini
a halo is a shining ring of light
a pod is a group of whales

explanation.surface: A mushroom ring glowing over a pod of whales, or perhaps a squid.
explanation.definitionFit: Squid belong to the cephalopods, the class including octopus and cuttlefish, so a squid is an example.

clue.text: Scent: ___ Cologne, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear says the blank is filled by a word that sounds like the answer

parts.note: the blank is the French eau de, as in eau de Cologne

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank perfume quiz.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic accent the scent word sounds like 'eau de', the start of eau de Cologne.
explanation.definitionFit: Odour is a smell, and scent is a synonym.

clue.text: Sharp work recalled in poet Hughes

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the word for work runs backwards

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
Ted Hughes was the English Poet Laureate

explanation.surface: A cutting piece of writing recalled from the poet Ted Hughes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns OP into PO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pointed has a sharp tip, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Quiet man, he struggling to get to grips with uprising one wonders?

parts.note: p, piano, means quiet in music

indicators.note: to get to grips with means to grab hold of, so the jumbled letters enclose the turned word
struggling means the letters of man and he writhe into a new order
uprising in a down clue means the word one reads upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A quiet man struggles to deal with an uprising: one wonders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' turns MAN HE into HMENA, which holds ENO, ONE turned by 'uprising'.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are remarkable things or people, wonders.

clue.text: Dislike assembling parts? Don't go there!

indicators.note: parts means a piece of the words, so the run is within dislike assembling

explanation.surface: If you hate putting flatpack bits together, avoid the place.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface joke is that this shop sells furniture you must assemble yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: IKEA is the Swedish flatpack furniture store, which a hater of self-assembly should avoid.

clue.text: Classic body, nothing less, there getting jiggly

indicators.note: getting jiggly means being shaken about, so the letters are mixed
less means without, so a letter comes out of body

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A classic figure, without nothing, getting wobbly there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' takes O from BODY, giving BDY; 'getting jiggly' mixes BDY with THERE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby at Epsom is one of the five English Classics, the major flat horse races.

clue.text: Greek character seen going north, set off

indicators.note: going north in a down clue means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
noted means seen, observed

explanation.surface: A Greek figure seen heading north, setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going north' turns ETANOTED around.
explanation.definitionFit: To detonate a bomb is to set it off.

clue.text: Hold breath, drawing in last of air

indicators.note: drawing in means pulling something inside, so the breath word takes in a letter

parts.note: a gasp is a sudden breath

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word air

explanation.surface: Someone holds their breath, sucking in the last of the air.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp something is to hold it firmly; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Old queen for whom clear bandages stretch too much

indicators.note: bandages is a verb here: the clear word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: overt means open, plain to see
ex means former, old
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: An elderly monarch for whom a clear bandage is pulled too tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for whom' is a link; EXER goes inside OVERT after its R.
explanation.definitionFit: To overexert is to push yourself beyond your limits, straining too hard.

clue.text: Port right behind organ saving animal, one fighting for an environmental cause

definitions.text: one fighting for an environmental cause

indicators.note: behind means the port and right letter follow the first part
saving here means keeping safe inside, so the organ holds the animal

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing
a cow is an animal
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A port worker on the right side of an organ rescues an animal, a green campaigner.
explanation.definitionFit: An eco-warrior is an activist who campaigns, sometimes militantly, to protect the environment.

clue.text: Gas explosion with fuse, both ends lit

indicators.note: both ends means the final letters of the two preceding words, explosion and fuse

parts.note: a light that is lit is on

explanation.surface: A gas blast set off by a fuse burning at both ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both ends' looks like the two ends of the fuse but takes the last letters of 'explosion' and 'fuse': N and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is a noble gas, element 10, used in glowing signs.

clue.text: Rest more than enough to secure promotion to the Premiership? A thousand banked

indicators.note: banked means put away inside, so the letter is placed within the victories

parts.words: more than enough to secure promotion to the Premiership?
parts.note: forty league wins in a season would be more than enough to win promotion to English football's Premiership
K stands for a thousand

explanation.surface: A football side takes a break after enough victories to go up, with a grand in the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The Premiership is England's top football league.
explanation.definitionFit: Forty winks is a short nap, a rest.

clue.text: Chamber stood for reform, not fighting

indicators.note: for reform says these letters are to be formed anew in another order

explanation.surface: A parliamentary chamber stands up for reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for reform' asks for CHAMBER STOOD rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Hors de combat is French for out of the fight, used of a soldier disabled or out of action.

clue.text: Clear — ship must turn round

indicators.note: must turn means the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Clear the decks: the ship must turn round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear' looks like the definition but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Spherical means shaped like a ball, round.

clue.text: A degree — is it the value of a coordinate?

parts.note: BSc, Bachelor of Science, is a degree
it, like SA, is sex appeal

explanation.surface: A student asks whether a degree is the measure of a coordinate.
explanation.definitionFit: The abscissa is the x-coordinate of a point, its distance along the horizontal axis.

clue.text: Top of chest, part receiving admiring glances, for starters

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the split word holds the letters

parts.note: to cleave is to split, part

indicators.note: for starters picks the first letters of admiring and glances

explanation.surface: Part of the upper chest that draws appreciative looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleavage is the hollow between the breasts at the top of the chest.

clue.text: Labour leader breaking old British PM's nose, you might say, showing proof of fitness

parts.note: a bird's bill could be called its nose

indicators.note: breaking means bursting into, so a letter splits the old leader's name

parts.note: Edward Heath was a Conservative Prime Minister in the 1970s; the possessive reads as of plus his surname

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of Labour

explanation.surface: A Labour leader breaks a former Tory premier's nose, proof he is fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM's nose' reads as the nose of the PM: BILL OF HEATH, with L placed in HEATH.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean bill of health is an official certificate or verdict that someone is well.

clue.text: Block, one accommodating me, inferior to farm building

indicators.note: inferior to means placed below, so in a down clue these letters come under the farm building

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, so me holds the letter inside

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A block of housing, one with me in, lower than the barn.
explanation.definitionFit: To stymie is to block or thwart someone.

clue.text: Unfortunate gift, greed — man, one's attracted to the food store!

definitions.text: one's attracted to the food store!

indicators.note: unfortunate suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An unlucky present and greed: a man drawn to the pantry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunate' mixes GIFT GREED MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A fridge magnet clings to the refrigerator, where food is stored.

clue.text: Vulgar youth listening to TV?

indicators.note: listening to says the letters of TV are taken as heard, by their sound

parts.note: said aloud, the two letters of TV are tea and vee; cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A loutish teenager glued to the telly.
explanation.walkthrough: The T of TV is heard as 'tea', and tea is CHA (British slang, from Chinese); the V stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Chav is British slang, often derogatory, for a brash, loutish young person.

clue.text: Kitchen implement keeping one on seat, baby calmer?

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the kitchen tool contains the other letters

parts.note: a grater is a kitchen tool for shredding
I is the Roman numeral for one
a pew is a church seat

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget holding someone on a chair, to soothe a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link: I goes beside PEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Gripe water is a remedy given to soothe colicky infants.

clue.text: Bugger duck sauce!

parts.note: a bugger is a nuisance, a pest
a duck in cricket is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An expletive, damn the duck sauce!
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian sauce of basil, pine nuts and cheese.

clue.text: Late news, in short?

parts.note: late means dead, so news of the late is a death notice, and in short asks for its clipped form

explanation.definitionFit: An obit is the abbreviated form of obituary, the notice reporting a recent death.

clue.text: Chain Hitler's men required to restrain old comedian

indicators.note: restrain means hold in, so the two letters enclose the comedian

parts.note: the SS were Hitler's paramilitary force
Jimmy Tarbuck is a veteran British comedian and TV host

explanation.surface: Nazi guards needed to hold back a veteran comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Starbucks is an international chain of coffee shops.

clue.text: One not putting down roots, no bananas

parts.note: going bananas is going mad

explanation.surface: A rootless person says no to bananas.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad wanders from place to place without settling.

clue.text: Support a black and white drink that's knocked over

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black on pencils

indicators.note: knocked over means tipped upside down, so the drink is read backwards

parts.note: a latte is a milky, white coffee

explanation.surface: A black and white drink is spilt, and someone is supporting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns LATTE into ETTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Abettal is the act of abetting, giving help or encouragement, a rare noun.

clue.text: Dirty old Italian well blocked with odd bits of sock

indicators.note: blocked with means stuffed with, so the Italian word takes letters inside

parts.note: bene is Italian for well

indicators.note: odd bits of picks the first and third letters of sock

explanation.surface: An old Italian well gets clogged with scraps of a dirty sock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits of' picks S and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means indecent or filthy, as dirty jokes are.
